errors.english: the path, the realization, the achievement of the method, and the nature of accomplishment
errors.why: These are the four standard aspects of the truth of the path: path (mārga), deliverance (nairyāṇika), reasoning/method (nyāya) and accomplishment (pratipatti); nges par 'byin pa is deliverance, not realization.

fix.find: the path, the realization, the achievement of the method, and the nature of accomplishment

errors.english: These, along with the supreme adherence to ethical discipline and ascetic observances
errors.why: The eight are the desire-realm afflictions abandoned by seeing the path truth (a set that includes śīlavrataparāmarśa), not the acceptance and knowledge plus that view.

errors.english: [note: This refers to the purification of wrong views regarding morality and religious vows]
errors.why: Śīlavrataparāmarśa is itself the wrong view (holding rules and vows as supreme) that is abandoned, not a purification of wrong views.

errors.english: stains one line of text partially illegible
errors.why: The Tibetan is complete; 'one line of text partially illegible' is an artifact, not in the source.

fix.find: stains one line of text partially illegible

errors.english: Regarding the cultivation of the Truth of the Path, there are four aspects in the Desire Realm
errors.why: The whole side is seven-syllable verse, rendered throughout as running prose.

note: Generally follows the verse on the path of seeing, but the four aspects of the path truth are garbled, the eight abandoned afflictions are misconstrued, and a stray scribal remark ends the side.

errors.english: Therefore, his primordial wisdom should be examined through diligent realization.
errors.why: PV II.32 (anuṣṭheyagataṃ jñānam asya vicāryatām): his knowledge concerning what is to be practised should be examined; nan tan bya is 'what is to be practised', not 'diligent'.

fix.find: Therefore, his primordial wisdom should be examined through diligent realization.
fix.replace: Therefore, his knowledge concerning what is to be practised should be examined.

errors.english: knowing other objects is possible because there is no difference in their non-deceptive nature regarding the essential point
errors.why: This explains why examining other objects is impossible/pointless: whether he can know them makes no difference to his non-deceptiveness about the principal aim; the English turns it into an affirmation that such knowledge is possible.

errors.english: Because one seeks to engage with one who possesses knowledge
errors.why: The Tibetan says a knower is sought for the sake of what is to be practised; that purpose clause is dropped.

note: The argument of PV II.32-33 is followed in outline, but the key verse on knowledge of what is to be practised is mistranslated and one step of the reasoning is inverted.

errors.english: endowed with equanimity
errors.why: brtse ba is compassion/loving concern, not equanimity.

errors.english: "A person should apply this for the sake of the desired result."
errors.why: The convention-maker thinks 'I shall connect the person (who applies it) with the desired result'; the intent is the maker's, not an instruction to the user.

note: A sound rendering of the argument about mantras as conventions; one clear term error and one blurred intention.

errors.english: the cultivation of mindfulness
errors.why: dran pa here is memory (the recollection of former births that follows), not meditative mindfulness.

note: Faithful in its handling of the compassion and habituation arguments; only a minor term issue.

errors.english: between a person and a cow
errors.why: ba men is the gavaya (wild ox), the standard example alongside the cow (go-gavaya), not a person.

fix.find: between a person and a cow
fix.replace: between a gavaya (wild ox) and a cow

errors.english: A person is not the substantial cause of a cow
errors.why: The gavaya is not the substantial cause of the cow.

fix.find: A person is not the substantial cause of a cow
fix.replace: A gavaya is not the substantial cause of a cow

errors.english: A cause that exists at a specific time
errors.why: dus tha dad pa is a cause at a different time (temporally distinct), which is only a situational or continuum cause.

fix.find: A cause that exists at a specific time
fix.replace: A cause that is distinct in time

errors.english: The way heat follows and recedes from the copper shows a distinction in how it is sustained.
errors.why: The fire, a distinct thing ascertained as cause of the copper's liquidity by positive and negative concomitance (anvaya-vyatireka), is shown to be only its sustaining condition; the logical terms are lost.

errors.english: (kalala) embryo in its first week; oval stage
errors.why: nur nur po is the second embryonic stage (arbuda); kalala is mer mer po.

errors.english: the cause of the body arises either from the mind acting as a cooperative condition with another mind
errors.why: The body's cause acts as co-operating condition together with the mind's cause, i.e. a prior mind; the roles are muddled.

errors.english: Alternatively, only the nature of the result itself—such as fire or clay in their specific states—acts as the substantial cause for the situational states and the continuity of the cause.
errors.why: The sentence says situational and continuum causes such as fire and clay are called substantial causes only insofar as they have the nature of the result; the English reorders the relation.

note: The upādāna argument about body and mind is repeatedly misrendered (gavaya as 'person', temporal distinctness reversed, logical terms lost); not reliable without a specialist pass.

errors.english: # Chapter on Valid Cognition
errors.why: No chapter heading is on this side; the heading is invented.

errors.english: Is one attempting to establish the independence of speech itself
errors.why: rang dbang du bsgrub pa is an independent (svatantra) proof as opposed to a prasaṅga; the question is whether 'being a speaker' is used as a svatantra reason.

fix.find: Is one attempting to establish the independence of speech itself
fix.replace: Is 'being a speaker' itself intended as an independent proof (svatantra)

errors.english: if one does not analyze, one might find simple pleasure in mere scripture
errors.why: In a prasaṅga the property accepted by the opponent on mere scripture, attractive only while unexamined (avicāraramaṇīya), is stated as the probans; the English makes it a separate remark about enjoying scripture.

note: The svatantra/prasaṅga dilemma is misread at its opening and one clause is mis-segmented, though the rest of the argument is followed; an invented heading opens the side.
A faithful rendering of the argument against suffering being made by another, with sound notes.

errors.english: excluding conceptual thought (kalpana) mental fabrication or construction which apprehends a contradictory nature
errors.why: 'Non-erroneous' excludes cognition that is FREE of conceptual construction (rtog pa dang bral ba) yet apprehends a contradictory nature; conceptual cognition is already excluded by 'free of conception'.

fix.find: excluding conceptual thought (kalpana) mental fabrication or construction which apprehends a contradictory nature
fix.replace: excluding cognition free of conceptual construction (kalpanā) which apprehends a contradictory nature

errors.english: Is this not done to prevent valid cognition (pramana) reliable or valid means of knowledge from becoming erroneous?
errors.why: The objection is that it is stated so that one does not mistake that cognition for a pramāṇa, not to keep pramāṇa from becoming erroneous.

errors.english: Being seated in a boat sentence continues to next page
errors.why: 'sentence continues to next page' is an artifact, not in the source.

fix.find: Being seated in a boat sentence continues to next page

note: Readable treatment of 'non-erroneous' and the causes of sensory error, but the key point about what 'non-erroneous' excludes is reversed.
Accurate rendering of the Vigrahavyāvartanī verses and autocommentary on the infinite regress of pramāṇas.

errors.english: # To this it is said: if it lacks the capacity regarding its own self
errors.why: This is still the opponent speaking ('what you say shows that if it lacks capacity regarding itself...'), leading into his charge of inconclusiveness; the English inserts a heading and presents it as a reply.

errors.english: This clarifies that the point claiming "the eye is the very essence of seeing" is flawed due to an uncertain reason.
errors.why: The opponent's charge of an inconclusive reason, made to establish that the eye has the nature of seeing, cannot be made with the fire example; the English makes the eye-sees thesis the thing that is faulty.

note: The gone/not-gone application to fire is rendered well, but the dialectic at the opening is misassigned between opponent and respondent.
